newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close flat, outperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close flat, outperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds pared early losses to end little changed on Wednesday, outperforming U.S. issues, as a solid performance by the currency in the face of strong U.S. data helped boost prices, analysts said.

"The Canadian dollar was relatively stable today, hovering in that upper C$1.39 (US$0.9194) range. I think that imparted a little bit of a positive tone to the Canadian market," said Michael Gregory, a fixed-income economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers in Toronto.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond traded unchanged at C$108.00 to yield 7.308 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 5/32 to yield 7.11 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 20 basis points from 22 basis points.

Canadian and U.S. debt markets opened weaker this morning after the U.S. Federal Reserve reported industrial production rose 0.9 percent in March, compared with expectations of a 0.6 percent rise. The Fed also reported that capacity utilization rose to 84.1 percent.
The data increased speculation that the Fed would hike interest rates as early as May, putting pressure on both Canadian bond markets and the currency.
The Canadian dollar softened after the data, but it failed to break through the key C$1.3990 (US$0.7148) level.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.25 to C$101.75 to yield 6.748 percent. The U.S. bond fell 4/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 14 basis points from eight basis points on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.16 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.29 percent.
